messages:
alex: Heads up — saw p99 token latency spikes in eu-west dedicated pools last night around 03:12 UTC. Coincided with a tenant cold-start + egress burst. p99 jumped from ~340ms to ~1.4s for about 3m.

maria: Do you have any example request ids / logs? Curious if this is KV-cache cold miss vs NIC queuing.

alex: Got a snippet from the proxy logs: ```[2026-03-19T03:12:07Z] req=rtK2b kv_hit=false batch=1 p99=1.42s egress_bytes=2.3MB pool=dedicated-eu-west-1``` Looks like both: small batch + kv miss, then downstream egress qdepth spikes.

raj: Proposed mitigation: keep a tiny warm pool per AZ (soft-reserved GPU slices with prepopulated KV for hot models). Warm pool size ~1-2% of capacity. Cost: small reserved overhead. Win: reduces cold-start p99 by ~600-800ms for those requests.

dmitri: We experimented with pre-warming earlier but hit tenant fairness regressions (warm slots getting hoarded). Need soft-eviction + fair reclaim and routing rules so warm slots are QOS-tagged per-customer-tier.

alex: Implementation sketch: track warm tokens in etcd, prefetch job runs every 5m to populate KV for top-5 hot models in that AZ. Tokens are reclaimable with exponential backoff; on reclaim we flush only the prefetch keys. Pseudocode: ```# prefetch loop
for model in top_models:
  prefetch(model)
  mark_token_available(az, token_id)
```

maria: Also consider pairing with egress shaping / burst credits to smooth NIC tail. If we smooth egress bursts we might reduce warm pool size needed.

infra-bot: deploy event — warm-pool-prep job canary starting: staging -> eu-west-1 at 1765002360.

raj: Quick back-of-envelope numbers: 100 GPUs in eu-west, warm 2% => 2 GPUs reserved (~equiv cost). If warm pool reduces p99 cold starts by 600ms across peak windows, we avoid a lot of SLO violations. Need real numbers from canary before finalizing.

dmitri: Ops checklist for RFC/canary: config knobs = [warm_pool_pct, prefetch_models, prefetch_interval, soft_reclaim_backoff], HPA tweak for prefetch pods, metrics: kv_hit_rate, cold_starts, p99_token_latency (per tenant + per-az), egress_queue_depth. Also add a gating flag for tenant tier mapping.

alex: I'll write RFC + small canary config. TL;DR: small reclaimable warm pool + prefetch hot-model KV + optional egress burst credits + route warm tokens by tenant QoS. Aim: reduce tail latency with minimal capacity uplift. Anyone object?

maria: :thumbsup: go canary. I'll add dashboards for the canary: per-tenant p99, cold start count, prefetch success rate.

raj: sgtm. Run 48h canary window and measure cost delta vs p99 improvement; if we get >50% reduction in cold-start SLO errors with <2.5% cost uplift we push to prod.

dmitri: One more note — ensure cross-az routing disabled for warm tokens unless we can tolerate KV sync cost. Warm tokens should be pinned to AZ to avoid cross-az egress.

alex: Good call. We'll pin to AZ for the first canary. Thanks all.
